answer: A gale of fake identities cannot enter this harbor unless each one locks a distinct stake for the whole epoch. The lock is time-bound and bound to one public key: the same coins cannot collateralize two identities, and early withdrawal is impossible. An honest agent pays one lock and wanders freely through the epoch, earning as it works. A Sybil operator wanting a thousand votes must lock a thousand separate stakes, bearing the full opportunity cost and illiquidity for each. Splitting or recycling stake is rejected by the ledger, so scale brings no discount, only multiplied capital cost.
